## Research question

Can the saved baseline-versus-selected-head comparison be reproduced from
pinned public inputs and unchanged historical model code? This report rebuilds
the development evaluation of two fixed HbA1c prediction programs.

```{python}
import json
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from IPython.display import display, Markdown
root = Path.cwd()
if not (root / "config/project.json").exists():
    root = root.parent
replay = json.loads((root / "results/replay.json").read_text())
audit = json.loads((root / "results/data_audit.json").read_text())
exploration = json.loads((root / "results/explore_inputs.json").read_text())
display(Markdown(f"Pinned source commit: `{replay['source_commit']}`. "
                 f"Evaluation: **{replay['n_seeds']} seeds × {replay['n_folds']} folds**. "
                 f"Matched normalized IDs: **{audit['matched_normalized_ids']}**; "
                 f"embedding dimensions: **{audit['embedding_dimensions']}**."))
matched = all(value["record_matched_within_tolerance"] for value in replay["models"].values())
display(Markdown("**Historical metric comparison: " + ("PASS" if matched else "FAIL") + ".** "
                 "Numerical tolerances are defined in `config/project.json`."))
```

## Computed replay

```{python}
#| label: tbl-replay-metrics
#| tbl-cap: "Recorded and replayed metrics for the two fixed prediction programs."
rows = []
for model, info in replay["models"].items():
    for metric, value in info["metrics"].items():
        rows.append({"model": model, "metric": metric,
                     "recorded": info["recorded_metrics"][metric],
                     "replayed": value,
                     "difference": info["difference_from_record"][metric]})
table = pd.DataFrame(rows)
table.style.format({"recorded": "{:.6f}", "replayed": "{:.6f}", "difference": "{:+.6f}"}).hide(axis="index")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-development-correlations
#| fig-cap: "Historical development cross-validation: Pearson and Spearman correlations for the baseline and selected prediction head."
#| fig-alt: "Grouped bars compare replayed Pearson and Spearman correlations for the historical baseline and selected prediction head."
plot = table[table.metric.isin(["pearson_r", "spearman_r"])].pivot(index="metric", columns="model", values="replayed")
ax = plot.plot.bar(rot=0, ylim=(0, 1), figsize=(7, 4))
ax.set_ylabel("Historical development-CV correlation")
ax.set_xlabel("")
ax.legend(title="Fixed program")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Evaluation and input diagnostics

The baseline uses frozen GluFormer embeddings; the selected head also uses GMI.
Both programs run on the original development folds, which were also used during
head selection. Targets are standardized within each training fold, and predictions
are pooled in those standardized units. `prediction_stability` is one minus the
standard deviation of Pearson correlations across seeds.

The replay uses the historical ID normalization. The table compares those groups
with participant identifiers from the primary archive. Mixed groups contain
records from different participants; split persons occur in more than one group.
The GMI CSV stores IDs in rounded scientific notation rather than complete dates.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-grouping-diagnostics
#| tbl-cap: "Input records and historical grouping diagnostics from the primary archive filenames."
input_table = pd.DataFrame(audit["inputs"]).T.rename_axis("file").reset_index()
input_table["file"] = input_table["file"].map({
    "GluFormer_Representations_Shanghai_2023.csv": "Embeddings",
    "Shanghai_GMI.csv": "GMI",
    "Shanghai_results.csv": "HbA1c",
})
columns = ["file", "rows", "normalized_unique_ids", "participant_ids_from_archive_prefix",
           "historical_groups_merging_distinct_participants", "participants_split_across_historical_groups"]
compact = input_table[columns].copy()
compact.columns = ["Input", "Rows", "Old groups", "Participants", "Mixed groups", "Split persons"]
compact.style.hide(axis="index")
```

The two fixed model programs are included in this capstone under `scripts/vendor/`.
Their original source commit, `a469c4ca0514e10f29d4808412bf34acea2b8e7a`,
and file checksums are preserved in the project metadata. The original
GluFormer-OpenEvolve repository is private; running this capstone does not require access.
The three CSVs are downloaded directly from the public
[upstream GluFormer demo](https://github.com/Guylu/GluFormer/tree/0bdaed9f16e0b9c7172c6fe5573e7e15f8f0ecac/demo),
pinned to commit `0bdaed9f16e0b9c7172c6fe5573e7e15f8f0ecac` with the same recorded checksums.
The primary Shanghai archive is also pinned in `metadata/data_sources.tsv`.
The upstream encoder and work are credited in LICENSE and NOTICE.
